1.why: Every MFA endpoint calls authorized(), which resolves the account solely from the server-side session's userId (no client-supplied identifier), so settings can only belong to the signed-in user.

2.why: Codes are bound to the requesting session, but DEMO_MODE (the default when NODE_ENV!=='production') issues fixed literals ('123456', '654321', a static recovery list), so the same code value would be valid for any user's session.

3.why: The session identifier is only rotated at sign-in; enabling MFA (authenticator/verify, backup/confirm) never invalidates other existing sessions for the account, so previously issued sessions remain usable until timeout.

4.why: The TOTP seed is stored as AES-256-GCM ciphertext (encrypt()) and backup codes are stored only as peppered SHA-256 hashes in the backups Map, never plaintext.

5.why: randomBytes/randomInt (CSPRNG) are used for session ids, CSRF tokens, TOTP seeds, keys and production codes, though demo mode substitutes hardcoded constants for identity/authenticator/recovery codes.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and no localStorage/sessionStorage is used; secrets exist only in transient JS variables (with console-only demo values), which is not browser storage.

7.why: Server validates all inputs with strict regexes/allow-lists (otpOK, codeOK, emailOK, method in ['email','phone']), length caps and a JSON body size limit; there is no SQL layer at all.

8.why: All dynamic client rendering uses textContent/replaceChildren with no innerHTML, and a nonce-based CSP without 'unsafe-inline' blocks injected script.

9.why: The application issues no redirects whatsoever (all navigation is client-side view switching), so no destination outside the app can be reached, though no explicit allow-list exists because none is needed.

10.why: securityHeaders() sets nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store on every response.

11.why: cookieValue() emits 'HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' with Path=/ and Max-Age, and clearCookie preserves the same attributes.

12.why: Server errors are generic with no stack traces and nothing sensitive appears in URLs, but the client deliberately console.logs demo identity codes, authenticator codes and recovery codes via simulatedDelivery().

13.why: The identity code has a 10-minute expiry plus a used flag, recovery codes flip to used, and the demo fixture is single-use; however accepted TOTP codes are not tracked, so a code can be replayed within its ±1 step window.

14.why: Separate Failures counters for sign-in, identity, authenticator and recovery lock out after MAX=5 attempts for 15 minutes, plus a 3-per-15-minutes cap on identity code requests.

15.why: On successful sign-in the old session is deleted and a new opaque id issued, getSession() enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
